### 2026-10-24 – # Made all of the Schematics of the MIDI Keyboard

**0.97h**

# Made all of the Schematics of the MIDI Keyboard

I just made the whole schematics of the keyboard, I was just doing the demo project, so it won't look very different to the tutorial. However, I do have a twist in mind of how I will make the capacitive keys.

Originally, I thought I would use the XIAO esp32 for budget purposes. I did it in the first Lapse. But then I realised, why not I use the Waveshare. It has more pins, they are ALL compatible with capacitive touch and so what if they are just a little bit more expensive. So, that's what I did in the second Lapse.

**Let's just hope the project is within the budget. Fingers crossed.**

You can see in the first screenshot, the final schematics I have produced.

### 2026-10-24 – # Transferred the schematics onto PCB and prepped for routing.

**5.35h**

# Transferred the schematics onto PCB and prepped for routing.

I transferred the schematics onto the PCB. Then I got started on my making of capacitive keys. If you see like little to no progress in the 1st Lapse. That is because I was making the Capacitive Keys in another window KiCad had already opened. So that's why. Before I got to this Hexagon shape, I was thinking about making like a cool **Tetris theme Capacitive keys** with the bricks layered out but then I thought that my fat fingers might press like 1 big key and 1 small keys, it won't work that well. So, then I stuck to the Hexagon.

## Importing the Capacitive Keys onto the PCB.

I realized that my current ones were FAR too small, so then I just kept tweaking the size so it is fairly proportionate to the other parts. EASY👍✅

## Reordering the parts around
After I got the size right, I just shuffled the parts around wherever I think it would look cool. I didn't want mine to be a carbon copy of the DEMO, so I changed mine to have like a **U** shape/wrap around the Capacitive keys.

## Swapping pins and preparing for routing

After that I learned from my previous mistake from Starbie. I reordered the pins from the schematic and updated it constantly to make the routing as seamless as possible. Took a while of tweaking because midway, I decided to change the layout slightly, so I had to reorder everything again to make routing easier.

## Routing the actual board
I started routing, at first it was going fairly well, they were connecting and everything, BUT. That's when I realised that other red wires were blocking the other wires from connecting, and then I didn't know about VIA's and then everything started looking like spaghetti.

BUT. I looked at the tutorials, researched on google, watch YT tutorials, then I got it. I tightly packed everything, realtered the pin layout ONCE AGAIN. and finally I got it. You can see, I got that fully systematic approach. Closer items at the bottom of the pin layout and further ones go on top. Oh yeah, I am so proud. I looked into VIAs and they proved to be REALLY HELPFUL, everything fitted so well. My best yet.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/01dbac6ce91ae6f6944f54c0a1ed95ba7d4cad61fc6bbbd2ad748407f09807ec.png)

## Adding the silkscreen decorations

I do admit, I have to declare an extra 90 mins for the making of the silkscreen decor. I just took screenshot of the official Hackclub/Halflife logos, put them in piskleapp.com edited them. Removed background, resized them, made them black and white and then imported them into KiCad's image converter. I adjusted the size of the icons and fitted them on. Sound's fairly simple, but it was HELLA tedious. so many pixels. this screenshot was the final product after I did all of the edits.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/H1UNfKeiXo6fn4gM7gioqmiooX6DUU7w/9179037070ac4c1e8bc54487e6bf6716cb74ffb0d2dd098f92ed263d3ec76f83.png)

I think I am nearly done. I have to import the 3D models, export it, finishing touches and make assemble the repository.
